title: Performance of a domain-specific large language model in answering patient questions in psychiatry
abstract: arXiv:2608.22797v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Background This study was designed to evaluate whether a domain-specific large language model (LLM) trained exclusively on patient education resources can answer questions about psychiatric medications, in a manner superior to LLM chatbots. We developed an LLM ("MIND") fine-tuned for clinical fidelity, trained on patient education resources from authoritative medical organizations. Methods We compared the responses of MIND, ChatGPT, and OpenEvidence to patient questions about escitalopram, using two methods: (1) computer analysis according to a rubric measuring accuracy, clarity, completeness, nuance, safety, and referral appropriateness; (2) ratings from N=10 board-licensed psychiatrists on similar metrics. Results When rated by rubric, MIND was rated highest in all domains (p<0.001). translated_title: 领域特定大语言模型在回答精神科患者问题中的表现
translated_abstract: 摘要：本研究旨在评估一个仅基于患者教育资源训练的领域特定大语言模型（LLM）在回答精神科药物相关问题方面是否优于通用LLM聊天机器人。我们开发了一个针对临床保真度微调的LLM（“MIND”），该模型基于权威医疗组织的患者教育资源进行训练。方法：我们通过两种方法比较了MIND、ChatGPT和OpenEvidence对艾司西酞普兰患者问题的回答：（1）根据评估准确性、清晰度、完整性、细微性、安全性和转诊适当性的评分标准进行计算机分析；（2）由10名持牌精神科医生在类似指标上进行评分。结果：在评分标准评估下，MIND在所有领域均获得最高分（p<0.001）。在精神科医生评分中，ChatGPT的准确性评分高于MIND，但效应量极小（p=0.021, r=0.073）；MIND在完整性方面评分更高。
tldr: 该研究开发了一个领域特定精神科LLM（MIND），在标准评估中表现优于通用模型，但精神科医生评分显示其准确性略低于ChatGPT，完整性更高。
en_tdlr: This study developed a domain-specific psychiatric LLM (MIND) that outperformed general models in rubric-based evaluations, but psychiatrist ratings showed slightly lower accuracy than ChatGPT with higher completeness.
